chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muammar ibn Khallad who said:

A man asked me to seek permission for him to enter upon him (meaning al-Rida, peace be upon him), and to ask him to gift him a cloak and give him some of his silver coins. When I returned from the man, I encountered his messenger looking for me. When I entered upon him, he said: 'Where were you?' I said: 'I was with so-and-so.' He said: 'He wishes to come see me?' I said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' Then I glorified Allah. He said: 'Why do you glorify?' I said to him: 'I was with him just now regarding this matter.' He said: 'Indeed, the believer is facilitated (for success). Then he said: 'If he comes to you, inform him.' He said: 'So when he entered upon him, he sat in front of him, and I stood in a corner. He called me and said: 'Sit,' so I sat. He asked him for supplication, which he did. Then he asked for a cloak. When he stood up, the Imam placed something in his hand. I looked and saw that it was coins from among his special coins.' Muhammad ibn Masud said: Ali ibn al-Hasan said: 'The man who asked for supplication and a cloak was al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt.' He also said: 'Al-Rayyan narrated this hadith to me.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the title of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida)
key_terms.مُوَقَّفٌ: Facilitated/Successful (referring to the believer's ease in matters)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt's visit to Imam al-Rida regarding his cloak and coins?
ai.summary: This narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the intuitive knowledge ('facilitation of the believer') and generosity of Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), who gifted the man a cloak and coins from his personal wealth after granting him supplication. The companion, identified as the prominent jurist al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, serves as a key witness, illustrating the Imam's accessibility and spiritual authority in Shia scholarly tradition. The event underscores the Imam's ability to discern the needs of his followers and bestow blessings, reinforcing the concept of divine facilitation in the life of the faithful.
